text.p: These are the leading stories in the Malawi press on Monday.
Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- A measles outbreak has killed nine children in Mulanje district, more than 60km east of Blantyre, the commercial city.

District Primary Health Officer Veronica Limwando said measles broke out between October and December last year and affected seven areas around the district with more than 130 cases recorded between July and September this year.

- An avalanche of mud-slide errupted at Livingstonia hill, in Rumphi district of northern Malawi, uprooted vegetation on 300-metre downhill and destroyed a two-and-half hectare of banana plantation, burying it under mud.

- Police fired in the air and teargassed the main opposition Malawi Congress Party (MCP) and the ruling United Democratic Front (UDF) supporters at Ndirande township in Blantyre when the two sides clashed on Sunday over a venue to hold campaign rallie

- Thousands of the main opposition Malawi Congress Party (MCP) supporters and officials were teargassed by police on Sunday and one official was stabbed during a clash with the ruling United Democratic Front (UDF) supporters.

- President Bakili Muluzi said in a Blantyre township that he is confident he will rule another term of five years as he sees no formidable opposition to prevent him a second run in 1999. He was touring Ndirande, Malawi's "Soweto" township in a runup to by-elections to be held on November 19.
